chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is upon the person in ihsar (state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah) to avoid the locusts if they are on his path, and if he finds no alternative, then he kills them, and there is no blame."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ritual consecration (Ihram) for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no blame or objection
key_terms.يَتَنَكَّبَ: To avoid or keep away from

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing locusts while in the state of Ihram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of minor disruptions to ihram, distinguishing between intentional violation and necessity (darura). It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the penalty (kaffarah) is waived for accidental or necessary acts, such as clearing a path blocked by swarms of locusts, thereby balancing ritual purity with practical ease during pilgrimage.
